relations.subject: tool:server-developer-tools-package
relations.evidence: The Server developer tools package lets you install the following EE Server utilities on the systems where you have not installed Couchbase Server:

notable_absence.finding: The developer tools package sentence explicitly gates itself to 'EE Server utilities', but the very next section describing the parallel admin tools package ('The Server admin tools package lets you install the following Server utilities...') drops the EE qualifier entirely for a structurally identical packaging pattern, even though it bundles cbbackupmgr (an EE-only tool elsewhere in the registry). No edition note is given for the admin package at all - an inconsistency in a page this procedural/table-driven, consistent with the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis of lighter TW review on cli/ pages.

cross_component_finding: This intro page's own content is almost entirely outbound links into other directories (backup-restore/, tools/, n1ql/, install/, cbcli/) rather than material native to cli/ - the 'CLI Reference' is a virtual, cross-cutting index over tools whose own reference pages live elsewhere in the tree, not a component with content of its own. Combined with cbstats-intro.md and cbepctl-intro.md (this batch's other two intro pages), the three are genuinely non-overlapping: this page indexes the whole CLI surface and its packaging/versioning, while the other two are each the top-level page for one tool-family's own subcommand tree - three different scopes, not three redundant overviews of the same thing.
cross_product_finding: The page's entire framing (install-location tables per OS, downloadable per-platform tarballs/zips, non-root install caveats) assumes an on-premises Server install; nothing on the page flags that Capella customers have no equivalent local binary install path, since Capella does not expose OS-level package management to customers.
